01-parallel-coords-sparkline-table.visual_critic_note: Intentional Paul Tol color palette, clean card layout with real typographic hierarchy, and the canvas+SVG layered parallel coords paired with a live sparkline table shows deliberate design — held back from 8 by the parallel coords being visually dense at full 150-line selection, making patterns hard to extract before brushing.
01-parallel-coords-sparkline-table.encoding_integrity_note: Data-driven domains via d3.extent, zero-baseline sparkline histograms with stable global bins, no radius deception, correct key function on table rows — minor deduction for hardcoded thresholds(24) instead of Sturges'/Scott's rule.
flags: Update Storm (minor): drawStrums() called synchronously on every pointermove outside RAF coalescing, causing unthrottled SVG DOM mutations during strumming
01-parallel-coords-sparkline-table.stress_test_note: Strong implementation — canvas rendering, RAF coalescing via dirty-flag pattern, pointer events unifying mouse/touch, and brush .filter() blocking Shift+drag — but drawStrums() bypasses the RAF gate and mutates SVG on every pointermove event.
01-parallel-coords-sparkline-table.cognitive_load_note: Two linked views, 6 colors, 150 lines managed well via canvas alpha-layering (0.1 unselected / 0.5 selected) — readable at rest but the parallel-coords mid-section tangles under full-data load and perceptual evaluation of brush/strum animation quality requires live interaction.
